 Damian W Betebenner & Adam VanIwaarden

BACKGROUND

 • 2016 Marked the 2nd year of PARCC test administration
 allowing for the calculation of student growth.

 • The growth model designated to be used for calculation was
 student growth percentiles (SGP).

 • The Center for Assessment was contracted to perform SGP
 analyses for 2016.

 • Preparation for SGP analyses began in May, 2016 leading up to
 nal SGP analyses being conducted in mid-July 2016

 content area in Spring 2016

• A total of 15,642 unique students received SGPs for at least 1 grade/content

• SGPs are calculated based upon test results for students taking the same tests

BACKGROUND

• SGPs are uniformly distributed and uncorrelated with prior achievement: All
 students, regardless of starting point can demonstrate high/low growth.

• Median SGP for consortium and state norm groups are 50.

• Tests of uniformity and the existence of ceiling effects are performed for each
 SGP norm-group analysis run.

• Scaled Score CSEMs provided by Pearson were incorporated for calculation of
 SGP SEMs.

• For testing purposes, scale score based SGPs, student growth projections
 (adequate growth percentiles) and SIMEX adjusted SGPs were calculated.

RESULTS

 • All analyses successfully completed mid July.

 • All state and consortium level analyses required approximately 24 hours to
 complete.

 • Goodness of t results were generally quite good (i.e., uniform distribution of
 SGPs by prior achievement) with no indications of ceiling/ oor effects.

 • Consortium-based median SGPs (by state, grade and content area) ranged
 from 40 to 60.

 • In some cases SGPs could be calculated at the consortium level but not the
 state level due to insuf cient numbers of students in the state norm group.
